authority: CEO Round 156: 'Every candidate with a proposed competitor comparison must define: baseline / public evidence / fidelity / uncertainty / metric / meaningful_difference / WIN threshold provenance / KILL threshold provenance. No unexplained thresholds.'
constitutional_basis: Article I — evidence precedes assertion (threshold must have evidence chain before experiment)
Article IV — no fallback epistemology (cannot weaken baseline to make candidate look better)
Article VII — never weaken verifier to rescue claim (cannot lower threshold after the fact)
Article XXVII — no threshold invention (every threshold needs provenance + class + uncertainty + justification)
Article XXIX — separate implementation failure from mechanism failure (baseline reproduction that underperforms published number = implementation failure, not incumbent weakness)
Article XXXII — state strongest alternative explanation (incumbent may have internal capability we cannot see)

C2_Y_CONTRACT.candidate: C2-Y: Longitudinal Shunt Response-Manifold Failure Prediction
C2_Y_CONTRACT.baseline_system: Best-plausible incumbent intelligent shunt = UNION OF publicly demonstrated capabilities from (a) VIEshunt adaptive control (posture→reference adjustment→ICP regulation+acute perturbation response) + (b) Nature 2026 ICP monitor (chronic long-term pressure trending with home monitoring) + (c) Codman/Medtronic-style threshold-based alerting (ICP > X mmHg → alarm). This is NOT a strawman single-product baseline. It is the strongest combination of publicly demonstrated capabilities that a well-resourced incumbent could plausibly assemble from public knowledge.
baseline_capabilities: Acute perturbation response to CSF bolus [DEMONSTRATED — VIEshunt]
Continuous long-term ICP measurement [DEMONSTRATED — Nature 2026, PMID 41927547]
Home monitoring with stable readings over follow-up [DEMONSTRATED — Nature 2026]
Threshold-based alarm when ICP crosses fixed boundary [DEMONSTRATED — Codman/Medtronic, marketed]
Patient posture tracking via IMU [DEMONSTRATED — VIEshunt]
Wireless data transmission [DEMONSTRATED — both VIEshunt and Nature 2026]

best_public_evidence.citation: VIEshunt intelligent electromechanical shunt, ETH Zurich / University Hospital Zurich, 2025
best_public_evidence.demonstrated: Acute ovine study; posture-dependent ICP regulation; CSF bolus perturbation response
best_public_evidence.limitation: Acute only; no chronic/longitudinal data; no failure prediction
best_public_evidence.epistemic_status: DEMONSTRATED for acute control + UNKNOWN for chronic prediction

best_public_evidence.demonstrated: 20-patient first-in-human safety; long-term pressure monitoring; stable readings; some shunt failure detection
best_public_evidence.limitation: Detection is post-hoc (failure has already occurred). No prediction. No classification.
best_public_evidence.epistemic_status: DEMONSTRATED for monitoring + basic failure detection + UNKNOWN for prediction/classification

best_public_evidence.citation: Codman ICP Express, Medtronic Codman, Integra Neuroscience
best_public_evidence.demonstrated: Threshold-based ICP alarming in clinical use for decades
best_public_evidence.limitation: Fixed thresholds; no learning; no failure-mode classification

implementation_fidelity.what_we_will_reproduce: All three baseline components above will be implemented as a unified reference baseline in the virtual cohort: (a) VIEshunt-style adaptive controller with posture-dependent reference trajectory + PI control on ICP error, (b) Nature-style long-term ICP sensor with realistic drift + noise model, (c) Codman-style threshold alarm at clinically standard 15 mmHg / 20 mmHg / 25 mmHg levels.
implementation_fidelity.what_we_CANNOT_reproduce: VIEshunt-specific micro-pump dynamics (proprietary). Nature 2026 sensor-specific noise spectrum (not fully published). We will use published noise/drift figures where available and labeled MODEL_DERIVED ranges where not.
implementation_fidelity.fidelity_class: HIGH for control architecture + MEDIUM for sensor model + MODEL_DERIVED for component-specific dynamics
implementation_fidelity.calibration_plan: Tune controller gains to reproduce VIEshunt-published ICP error response to perturbation (paper Figure 4-5). If reproduction underperforms published response by >20%, baseline implementation is INCOMPLETE per Article XXIX and the experiment is BLOCKED until fidelity is achieved.
implementation_fidelity.adversarial_self_attack: Per Article XVII: an intelligent adversary would tune the baseline controller WEAKLY to make C2-Y look better. Counter: controller gains are pre-registered and frozen BEFORE C2-Y is run. Any controller tuning after C2-Y results are known is forbidden (Article XIX).

known_uncertainty.correct_language: NO_PUBLIC_EVIDENCE of VIEshunt chronic performance; cannot claim 'VIEshunt fails chronically' — only 'no published evidence of chronic capability'
known_uncertainty.implication_for_baseline: We model VIEshunt-like control assuming controller behavior is stable over the test horizon. If chronic drift would degrade VIEshunt, that is a separate finding, not a baseline assumption.

known_uncertainty.epistemic_status: PARTIALLY_DEMONSTRATED (paper mentions 'some shunt failures detected' but algorithm not published)
known_uncertainty.correct_language: DEMONSTRATED that some failures were detected; UNKNOWN what algorithm; we use threshold-based detection as best-plausible baseline

known_uncertainty.epistemic_status: HYPOTHETICAL (no one has publicly integrated these)
known_uncertainty.correct_language: This is a BEST-PLAUSIBLE incumbent, not a real product. The incumbent may have internal R&D we cannot see (Article XXXII).

metric_definition.mathematical_definition: Lead time (hours) = t_clinical_failure - t_first_alarm, conditioned on the false-alarm rate being <= FPR_target over the patient-month horizon. The fixed FPR target is pre-registered.
metric_definition.why_lead_time_at_fixed_FPR_not_lead_time: Lead time alone is gameable: an over-sensitive alarm gives high lead time but unacceptable false alarms. Conditioning on fixed FPR forces the candidate to earn its lead time through specificity, not through alarm spamming.
secondary_endpoints: false_alarms_per_patient_month at the lead-time operating point
failure_mode classification accuracy (obstruction vs overdrainage vs underdrainage vs valve dysfunction vs posture artifact)
robustness_index (lead-time degradation under sensor drift / model mismatch / patient transfer)

clinical_decision.decision_the_alert_triggers: Outpatient surgical evaluation within the lead-time window. NOT emergency surgery — the value is that lead time converts ED presentation into scheduled revision.
clinical_decision.decision_threshold: Alert → imaging (CT shunt series) → if imaging confirms → OR within 24h. Without lead time, current practice is emergent ED presentation → emergent revision.
clinical_decision.who_decides: Neurosurgeon + neurology; alert is advisory, not autonomous
clinical_decision.regulatory_frame: FDA SaMD (Software as a Medical Device) Class II likely; CDSI guidance applies

minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_for_lead_time: ≥8 hours — because the clinical workflow delta is: (i) 8h allows next-day scheduled OR rather than emergent overnight OR; (ii) <8h is operationally indistinguishable from ED presentation
minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_for_false_alarms: ≤2 false alarms per patient-month — because alarm fatigue literature shows >2 alarms/month causes clinician desensitization (.Sendelbach et al. Am J Crit Care 2015;24strpos)
minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_for_classification: ≥20 percentage point improvement over baseline — because classification accuracy below this is dominated by class imbalance (obstruction is most common; trivially predicting 'obstruction' gives ~60%)
minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_provenance_class: CLINICAL (workflow + alarm fatigue literature) + ENGINEERING (class imbalance)
minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_uncertainty: MEDIUM — the 8h workflow delta is plausible but not directly validated for shunt patients specifically. The 2 FA/month threshold comes from cardiac alarm literature, transferred to neurosurgery.

statistical_power_requirement.effect_size_assumed: Lead-time difference of 12h between C2-Y and baseline (above the 8h MMD)
statistical_power_requirement.n_per_arm: n = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.84) * 8 / 12)^2 = ~11 patients per arm. We will use n=30 per arm for robustness to non-normality and to power the secondary endpoints.
statistical_power_requirement.virtual_cohort_size: 300 virtual patients (allows stratification by failure mode × patient variability × sensor-noise level)
statistical_power_requirement.multiple_testing_correction: Bonferroni across 5 failure modes — adjusted alpha 0.01 per mode
statistical_power_requirement.pre_registration: Power analysis pre-registered in C2_Y_POWER_ANALYSIS.json BEFORE the experiment runs

thresholds.false_alarms: <= 1 FA/patient-month at the lead-time operating point

provenance_chain.source: Hydrocephalus Association patient education + neurosurgical clinical practice: typical shunt failure progression from symptomatic to severe is 24-72h. 24h is the minimum actionable window for outpatient surgical scheduling.
provenance_chain.uncertainty: MEDIUM — derived from clinical practice, not RCT. No trial has measured the clinical value of specific lead-time durations.
provenance_chain.rationale: Anything below 24h provides limited operational benefit over current emergent presentation. 24h is the minimum that changes workflow.

provenance_chain.source: Sendelbach & Halm 2015 Am J Crit Care + clinical alarm fatigue literature: >2 alarms/month leads to clinician desensitization. We set the bar more conservatively at 1/month because (a) pediatric shunt patients have decades of expected life with the device, (b) repeated false alarms in children cause parental anxiety and unnecessary imaging.
provenance_chain.uncertainty: MEDIUM — alarm fatigue literature is cardiac-monitor-derived; transferred to neurosurgical shunt context.
provenance_chain.rationale: 1/month balances sensitivity against the chronicity of pediatric hydrocephalus. 0/month would force sensitivity too low; 2/month risks alarm fatigue.

provenance_chain.source: Trivial classifier predicting 'obstruction' gives ~60% (class imbalance). 70% is 10pp above trivial — minimum for the classification to carry decision value (i.e., the alert would change management).
provenance_chain.uncertainty: LOW — class imbalance is well-documented in shunt failure literature.
provenance_chain.rationale: Below 70%, the classification adds no actionable information beyond 'alert: something is wrong'.

thresholds.lead_time: < 4h at FPR_target = 1 FA/patient-month — operationally indistinguishable from no warning
thresholds.false_alarms: > 3 FA/patient-month — alarm fatigue threshold from literature, above which clinician desensitization is documented
thresholds.classification_accuracy: < 50% — below chance for 5-class problem with class imbalance correction

provenance_chain.source: Neurosurgical workflow: emergent presentation to OR typically takes 4-8h. If C2-Y provides <4h lead time, the patient still presents emergently. The invention provides no operational value.
Alarm fatigue literature; also FDA guidance on alarm system safety. Above 3 FA/month, the alerting system is unsafe.
Below chance for the class-imbalance-adjusted baseline. The classification is no better than random.

C2_Y_CONTRACT.intermediate_zone: If results fall between WIN and KILL on any primary threshold, C2-Y remains INCONCLUSIVE. The system must NOT silently promote an inconclusive result (Article XXVIII). The INCONCLUSIVE state requires either (a) a tightened experiment design that resolves the ambiguity, or (b) a public KILL with explicit rationale that the question was asked and not answered.
falsification_requirements: If C2-Y lead time <= 4h under the strongest plausible baseline, C2-Y is KILLED
If C2-Y cannot achieve >70% classification accuracy across all 5 failure modes, C2-Y is KILLED

If baseline reproduction underperforms published VIEshunt response by >20%, the experiment is BLOCKED until fidelity is achieved (Article XXIX) — this is NOT a C2-Y failure, it is a baseline-implementation failure

C3_X_CONTRACT.candidate: C3-X: Closed-loop CNS Therapeutic Delivery (CSF state → PK model → adaptive dosing → response monitoring)
C3_X_CONTRACT.baseline_system: TWO baselines, not one. Both must be beaten. (A) ThecaFlex-style open-loop fixed-dose intrathecal delivery [DEMONSTRATED — Biogen SEC filings, clinical studies]. (B) Best-practicable adaptive control baseline: PK-guided dosing where dose is adjusted by a Bayesian estimator of patient-specific clearance, with no CSF-state feedback. This is the strongest plausible adaptive baseline that does NOT require the C3-X invention.

baseline_A_ThecaFlex_open_loop.evidence: Biogen acquired Alcyone for ~$85M; ThecaFlex DRx in clinical studies (multiple trials referenced in Biogen 10-K)
baseline_A_ThecaFlex_open_loop.epistemic_status: DEMONSTRATED for open-loop hardware + dosing characterization

capabilities: Bayesian population PK model with patient-specific posterior [published PK literature]
Dose adjustment based on observed plasma/CSF drug levels [standard therapeutic drug monitoring]
Population-level covariate adjustment (weight, age, CSF flow rate) [published]
Therapeutic window targeting with target concentration intervention [TDM standard of care]
baseline_B_best_practicable_adaptive_con.evidence: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) is standard of care for many intrathecal therapies (baclofen, ziconotide, etc.). Bayesian dose adjustment is well-published (e.g., Beal et al. on NPCOMP).
baseline_B_best_practicable_adaptive_con.epistemic_status: DEMONSTRATED in adjacent therapeutic areas + UNKNOWN for the specific C3-X therapeutic target (because the C3-X target is not yet specified publicly)
baseline_B_best_practicable_adaptive_con.why_this_is_not_a_strawman: TDM with Bayesian adjustment is the standard-of-care adaptive approach. If C3-X cannot beat this, the closed-loop CSF-state-aware advantage is illusory. Using only ThecaFlex-style fixed-dose open-loop as the baseline would be the strawman the CEO warned against.
baseline_B_best_practicable_adaptive_con.what_we_will_reproduce: Implement Bayesian population PK with patient-specific posterior update from observed drug levels. Use published PK parameters for the chosen model drug (e.g., intrathecal baclofen). Pre-register the Bayesian model BEFORE C3-X runs.
baseline_B_best_practicable_adaptive_con.adversarial_self_attack: An adversary could weaken Baseline B by using a poor PK model or insufficient patient data. Counter: the PK model is pre-registered, frozen, and uses published parameter values. Any post-hoc weakening of Baseline B is forbidden (Article XIX).

best_public_evidence: Biogen 10-K (2025-2026) — ThecaFlex DRx acquisition + clinical pipeline
Alcyone Biomedical publications on ThecaFlex hardware
Therapeutic drug monitoring literature for intrathecal therapies (baclofen, ziconotide, methotrexate)
Bayesian dose adjustment: Beal, Sheiner, NONMEM methodology references

implementation_fidelity.what_we_will_reproduce: Baseline A: open-loop fixed-dose per ThecaFlex-published protocols. Baseline B: Bayesian population PK with NONMEM-style posterior update from observed CSF drug concentration at sampled timepoints.
implementation_fidelity.what_we_CANNOT_reproduce: Biogen-internal clinical data on ThecaFlex performance. We use published characterizations; where Biogen internal data would give different results, we mark those MODEL_DERIVED.
implementation_fidelity.fidelity_class: HIGH for Baseline A (open-loop is simple) + HIGH for Baseline B (Bayesian TDM is methodologically mature)
implementation_fidelity.calibration_plan: Validate Baseline B against published intrathecal baclofen PK data. If reproduction differs from published by >15%, baseline implementation is INCOMPLETE (Article XXIX).

known_uncertainty.component: ThecaFlex closed-loop intelligence (if any internal development)
known_uncertainty.epistemic_status: UNKNOWN — Biogen has not publicly disclosed any closed-loop dosing work for ThecaFlex. We must NOT assume 'ThecaFlex is open-loop' = 'Biogen cannot do closed-loop'. The correct language: 'NO_PUBLIC_EVIDENCE of closed-loop development'.
known_uncertainty.implication_for_baseline: Baseline A is open-loop because that's what's published. If Biogen has internal closed-loop work, our baseline is weaker than the true incumbent. Article XXXII: state this alternative explicitly.

known_uncertainty.epistemic_status: POTENTIALLY_NOVEL — no public system demonstrates CSF-state-feedback-controlled intrathecal dosing
known_uncertainty.implication: C3-X's potential moat is in the CSF-state feedback loop, NOT in the existence of intrathecal dosing hardware (ThecaFlex has that) or adaptive dosing (TDM has that).

metric_definition.mathematical_definition: Fraction of patient-time that CSF drug concentration is within [therapeutic_lower, therapeutic_upper] bounds. Also reported: CV of CSF drug concentration over the dosing horizon.
secondary_endpoints: patient_specific_optimization_benefit (per-patient improvement vs population-optimal fixed dose)

clinical_decision.decision_the_alert_triggers: Dose adjustment (increase, decrease, hold). The closed loop recommends a dose change; clinician approves before execution.
clinical_decision.decision_threshold: If model predicts concentration will exit therapeutic window in next 4h, recommend pre-emptive dose adjustment
clinical_decision.regulatory_frame: FDA CDSI guidance; likely Class II SaMD paired with the drug+device combination product

minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_for_CV: ≥30% relative reduction in CV vs Baseline A — because below 30% is within typical PK variability and not clinically distinguishable
minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_for_overdosing: ≥40% relative reduction in overdosing events — because intrathecal overdosing can be catastrophic (e.g., baclofen overdose → coma)

statistical_power_requirement.effect_size_assumed: 30% relative CV reduction (C3-X vs Baseline A)
statistical_power_requirement.virtual_cohort_size: 200 virtual patients (allows stratification by clearance phenotype, age, weight, CSF flow rate)

thresholds.vs_Baseline_A_ThecaFlex: C3-X concentration CV < 50% of Baseline A AND overdosing events reduced >60%
thresholds.vs_Baseline_B_adaptive_TDM: C3-X concentration CV < 70% of Baseline B AND overdosing events reduced >30%

provenance_chain.source: Bioequivalence criteria (FDA) typically require 80-125% range; we use 50% as the bar because the comparison is not bioequivalence but therapeutic advantage. A 50% reduction in CV is the minimum that translates to a clinically observable reduction in symptomatic over/under-dosing events.
Intrathecal baclofen overdose literature: ~5-15% of patients experience overdose events per year. 60% reduction moves this to 2-6%, which is a clinically meaningful safety improvement.

Best-practicable adaptive TDM should already achieve substantial CV reduction vs open-loop. C3-X must demonstrate ADDITIONAL improvement over adaptive TDM, not just over open-loop. 70% of Baseline B = 30% additional improvement, which is the MMD.
provenance_chain.uncertainty: MEDIUM — assumes Baseline B is well-implemented

thresholds.vs_Baseline_B: If C3-X concentration CV > 80% of Baseline B CV, C3-X provides no material advantage over adaptive TDM. KILLED.
thresholds.vs_Baseline_A: If C3-X does not significantly beat Baseline A on overdosing reduction (p > 0.05), C3-X provides no safety advantage. KILLED.

provenance_chain.source: Below 20% additional improvement is within typical cross-patient PK variability. The invention provides no measurable advantage over the standard-of-care adaptive approach.

provenance_chain.threshold: No significant overdosing reduction vs Baseline A = KILL
provenance_chain.source: If C3-X cannot demonstrate safety advantage over open-loop, the regulatory and clinical case for closed-loop collapses.

falsification_requirements: If C3-X beats Baseline A but not Baseline B, C3-X is INCONCLUSIVE — the invention may not provide advantage over best-practicable adaptive care
If Baseline B (Bayesian TDM) implementation underperforms published TDM results by >15%, baseline implementation is INCOMPLETE (Article XXIX) — not a C3-X failure

C5_X_CONTRACT.candidate: C5-X: Predictive Embolic-Risk Engine (validated precursor + patient-specific twin + intervention optimization)
C5_X_CONTRACT.baseline_system: THREE baselines, all must be beaten. (A) Best published physics-only predictor of thrombus fragmentation. (B) Best published data-driven (ML) predictor. (C) Best published combined physics+ML approach. The competitive white space is NOT declared empty until all three are characterized.

baseline_A_physics_only.description: Pure computational fluid dynamics + solid mechanics model of thrombus. Predicts fragmentation from stress/strain distribution. No learning component.
baseline_A_physics_only.best_public_evidence: PMID 41663082 (2026 thrombosis digital twin review) + earlier CFD-thrombus work (e.g., Bernsdorf et al., Thrombosis Research)
baseline_A_physics_only.epistemic_status: DEMONSTRATED in academic literature; no clinical product
baseline_A_physics_only.what_we_will_reproduce: Implement physics-only fragmentation predictor using our existing World A (FEBio) + World D (CalculiX) + World E (SfePy) infrastructure. Use published constitutive models for thrombus (hyperelastic + damage). Pre-register the model BEFORE C5-X runs.
baseline_A_physics_only.adversarial_self_attack: An adversary would implement a weak physics model. Counter: pre-register constitutive parameters from literature; freeze before C5-X runs.

baseline_B_data_driven.description: Pure ML predictor: features (clot geometry, flow conditions, patient history) → fragmentation risk. No physics.
baseline_B_data_driven.best_public_evidence: Recent ML thrombus characterization work (e.g.,-image-based DL for clot histology, Tang et al.); stroke embolus classification ML papers
baseline_B_data_driven.epistemic_status: DEMONSTRATED in academic literature; no clinical product
baseline_B_data_driven.what_we_will_reproduce: Train a gradient-boosted tree + dense NN on simulated virtual cohort data. Features: clot geometry (length, cross-section, taper), flow conditions (Re, WSS, residence time), patient covariates. Target: binary fragmentation event. Cross-validate. Pre-register feature set BEFORE C5-X runs.

baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.description: Hybrid: physics simulation produces features (stress fields, fragmentation energy) → ML combines with patient features for prediction.
baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.best_public_evidence: PMID 42508673 (2026 computational review) describes multiple physics+ML approaches for thrombosis
baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.what_we_will_reproduce: Use our World A FEBio simulation to extract stress/strain features, then train ML on (physics features + patient features) → fragmentation. This is the strongest plausible baseline.

best_public_evidence_summary: PMID 41663082 — 2026 thrombosis digital twin review (describes physics-only and physics+ML approaches)
PMID 42508673 — 2026 computational review (describes multiple ML+physics approaches)
Image-based ML for clot histology (multiple 2024-2025 papers)

implementation_fidelity.what_we_will_reproduce: All three baselines, using our existing multi-world infrastructure (FEBio, CalculiX, SfePy for physics; standard ML libraries for data-driven).
implementation_fidelity.what_we_CANNOT_reproduce: Specific academic group implementations (we don't have their code). We use published methods + parameters; deviations are MODEL_DERIVED.
implementation_fidelity.fidelity_class: HIGH for physics baselines (we have working FEBio/CalculiX/SfePy) + MEDIUM for ML baselines (we use standard libraries; specific architectures may differ from published)
implementation_fidelity.calibration_plan: For each baseline, validate against published benchmark cases. If reproduction underperforms published by >25%, baseline is INCOMPLETE (Article XXIX).
implementation_fidelity.adversarial_self_attack: An adversary would reproduce a weak version of each baseline. Counter: pre-register the model architecture + parameters from literature; freeze before C5-X runs.

known_uncertainty.correct_language: Cannot declare competitive white space empty until baselines are characterized (per CEO directive)

known_uncertainty.epistemic_status: POTENTIALLY_NOVEL — combination of (a) validated precursor (survives clotFoam) + (b) patient-specific twin + (c) intervention optimization
known_uncertainty.implication: C5-X's moat is in the COMBINATION + VALIDATION, not in any single component. Physics-only does (a) without (b)(c). Data-driven does (b) without (a)(c). Physics+ML does (a)(b) without (c) or without independent validation.

metric_definition.mathematical_definition: Reduction in embolic-risk events (simulated) when an intervention policy is chosen using C5-X predictions vs intervention policy chosen using each baseline, under a fixed intervention budget (e.g., max K interventions per N patients).
metric_definition.why_decision_benefit_not_AUROC_alone: AUROC alone is gameable: a predictor with high AUROC but poorly calibrated probabilities can lead to worse decisions under a constrained budget. The CEO directive explicitly requires decision benefit.
secondary_endpoints: transfer_across_conditions (train on condition X, test on condition Y)
uncertainty_quantification_quality (predicted vs actual coverage of confidence intervals)

clinical_decision.decision_the_alert_triggers: Selection of patients for invasive intervention (e.g., mechanical thrombectomy, clot retrieval) under constrained resources
clinical_decision.decision_threshold: If predicted fragmentation risk > threshold T, recommend intervention; if < T, defer. T is chosen to maximize true positives under intervention budget K.
clinical_decision.regulatory_frame: FDA SaMD; likely Class II if used for triage, Class III if used autonomously

minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_for_AUROC: ≥0.05 absolute AUROC improvement over best baseline — because below 0.05 is within typical cross-validation variance
minimum_meaningful_difference.MMD_for_decision_benefit: ≥10% relative reduction in embolic-risk events under intervention budget — because below 10% is operationally indistinguishable from the baseline policy

statistical_power_requirement.virtual_cohort_size: 500 virtual patients × 3 clot geometries × 3 flow conditions = 4500 cases (allows stratification + cross-validation)

thresholds.decision_benefit: >= 10% relative reduction in embolic-risk events under intervention budget
thresholds.independent_reproduction: C5-X prediction survives actual clotFoam execution (OpenFOAM-9, not just our internal World C flow simulator)
thresholds.intervention_quality: C5-X provides actionable intervention recommendation (not just risk score)

provenance_chain.class: CLINICAL + ENGINEERING (transferred from clinical prediction rule literature)
provenance_chain.source: High-stakes clinical prediction rules (e.g., stroke intervention decision aids) typically require AUROC >= 0.85 to be clinically actionable. CHADS-VASc (~0.72) is used for lower-stakes screening; thrombectomy triage demands higher.
provenance_chain.uncertainty: MEDIUM — transferred from adjacent clinical areas; not shunt/thrombus-specific

provenance_chain.source: Typical cross-validation variance in ML benchmarks. Improvements below 0.05 are within noise.
Health-economics literature on intervention triage: 10% relative reduction in events is the minimum that translates to a measurable QALY gain in cost-effectiveness analysis.

provenance_chain.class: ENGINEERING + CONSTITUTIONAL (Article XXVIII — no silent semantic promotion)
provenance_chain.source: Our World C flow simulator is custom Python. clotFoam (OpenFOAM-9) is an independent external solver. If C5-X prediction survives clotFoam, the prediction has independent physical reproduction. If it does not, the prediction is over-fit to our internal simulator.
provenance_chain.uncertainty: LOW — this is the constitutional requirement for independent reproduction

thresholds.independent_reproduction: Does not survive actual clotFoam (over-fit to internal World C)
thresholds.decision_benefit: No significant decision benefit over best baseline (p > 0.05)

provenance_chain.source: Below 0.70, the predictor is not clinically actionable for any high-stakes decision.
Article XXVIII (no silent semantic promotion): a model that survives only in its training simulator is not validated.

falsification_requirements: If any of the three baselines (physics-only, data-driven, physics+ML) cannot be reproduced within 25% of published performance, baseline implementation is INCOMPLETE (Article XXIX) — the experiment is BLOCKED
If C5-X does not beat all three baselines on AUROC AND decision benefit, C5-X is INCONCLUSIVE — the moat is not established
If C5-X does not survive actual clotFoam (independent solver), C5-X is KILLED regardless of other metrics (constitutional requirement)

summary_of_changes_vs_R155.R155_baseline_specs: Loose spec: 'WIN = >24h lead time + <1 FA/month' with no provenance
summary_of_changes_vs_R155.R156_contracts: Full 11-field contract per candidate, with threshold provenance chains (CLINICAL/ENGINEERING/MODEL_DERIVED/CONSTITUTIONAL classes), MMD justifications, statistical power requirements, falsification requirements, adversarial self-attacks
key_structural_changes: C2-Y baseline is now UNION of VIEshunt + Nature ICP monitor + Codman threshold alerting (best-plausible incumbent), not just VIEshunt alone
C3-X now has TWO baselines (ThecaFlex open-loop + Bayesian adaptive TDM), must beat BOTH
C5-X now has THREE baselines (physics-only + data-driven + physics+ML), must beat ALL THREE
Every threshold has explicit provenance class + source + uncertainty (Article XXVII)
Every contract has adversarial self-attack section (Article XVII)
Every contract has falsification requirements that distinguish C2-Y/C3-X/C5-X failure from baseline-implementation failure (Article XXIX)

honest_assessment.what_is_strong: The contract structure forces every threshold to have a provenance chain. The multi-baseline approach (esp. C3-X dual baseline and C5-X triple baseline) makes the strawman attack much harder.
what_is_still_weak: Several provenance chains are MODEL_DERIVED or transferred from adjacent clinical areas. We do not have direct RCT evidence for shunt-failure-prediction lead-time thresholds.
The 'best-plausible incumbent' for C2-Y is hypothetical — no real product integrates VIEshunt + Nature + Codman. The contract is honest about this.
Statistical power requirements use virtual cohort sizes; real clinical trial sizing would require different calculations.
what_we_are_NOT_claiming: We are NOT claiming these thresholds are correct. We are claiming they are EXPLICIT and TRACEABLE.
We are NOT claiming the baselines are real products. We are claiming they are the strongest plausible publicly-demonstrated combinations.
We are NOT claiming C2-Y/C3-X/C5-X will win. We are claiming the experiment is now well-defined enough that winning or losing is informative.
